meta.description: The 436 R&EM flight is the 436 AW Commander’s Air Force Emergency Management (EM) program office of primary responsibility (OPR) and is the Installation Office of Emergency Management. The flight executes and assists in the training and education of people and protection of assets before, during, and after disasters, major accidents, civil emergencies, humanitarian operations, terrorist events, or hostile action at either home station or at a deployed location. Protection for personnel includes all assigned military, civilian (Department of Defense [DOD] and contract personnel), dependents, and guests. Flight personnel provide on-scene and Emergency Operations Center (EOC) command and control (C2) support, specialized CBRN detection, identification, sampling and may support contamination control and decontamination operations. The R&EM Flight provides guidance to installation units to mitigate the effects of disasters and hostile incidents and to ensure rapid response to and recovery from these incidents.
meta.jhaNotes: The 436 CES/CEX Flight has CBRN Identification, detection, and Decontamination equipment that may be hazardous if not properly used, maintained, and stored.  Specific hazards include Calibration Gas, i.e. Carbon Monoxide, Chlorine, Nitrogen/Sulfur Dioxide, Nitrogen/Nitiric Oxide, Nitrogen/Anhydrous Ammonia. Reactive Skin Decontamination Lotion (RSDL). M-9 and M-8 CBRN detection Paper. Class 3B lasers. Radiological Test sources (cesium 137).

meta.medicalFacility:
For all Emergencies (life, limb or eyesight) dial 911. 

During normal duty hours on weekdays, personnel are to report to
Dover AFB Clinic for assessment and treatment of injuries suffered while on-the-job. Civilian employees may elect to receive treatment from their personal physician.
If the injury or medical condition does not permit the injured person to first report to Dover AFBClinic, the individuals should be treated at the closest medical facility which in most cases will beBay Health Medical Center (otherwise known as Kent General Hospital) located in downtown Dover, contact information is: (302) 674-4700.
The Base Clinic is located in Building 300. Also, advise member that the Base Clinic no longerprovides 24 hour emergency service. Make sure the individual understands the procedure to getmedical attention on and off duty as per TRICARE provider procedures (1-877-TRICARE or 1-877-874-2273).

selectedModules.title: Respiratory Protection Program
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train users before respirator use and at least annually on why the respirator is necessary, how improper fit or maintenance can compromise protection, and how to inspect, don, doff, use, and store the respirator.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Document fit testing and occupational health training on AF Form 2767 and ensure wearers understand emergency-use limits, cartridge change-out, cleaning, and medical qualification requirements.

selectedModules.title: CPR Training
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 1
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide CPR and AED training before assignment where required, and refresh qualification before expiration.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Ensure designated responders maintain current certification and understand location and use of local AED assets under the unit mishap prevention program.

selectedModules.title: Laser Safety Training
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide laser hazard awareness, eyewear, posting, alignment, and beam-control training before personnel work with lasers or enter laser-controlled areas.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use local laser safety officer guidance and approved operating instructions to cover exposure limits, alignment procedures, and emergency actions.
selectedModules.afTrainingBasis: DAFI 48-139 / Laser and Optical Radiation Protection

selectedModules.title: ALARA Ionizing Radiation Training
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train personnel on the ALARA concept, exposure minimization, posting requirements, and emergency actions before working with ionizing radiation sources.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use local radiation safety office guidance to cover dose control, exposure tracking, and access requirements for designated radiation areas.

selectedModules.title: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 14; 29 CFR Part 1910 - Occupational Safety and Health Standards (General Industry Standards) Subpart I; 29 CFR 1910.132; 29 CFR 1910.133; 29 CFR 1910.135; 29 CFR 1910.136; 29 CFR 1910.138
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train each affected worker on when PPE is necessary, what PPE is necessary, how to properly don, doff, adjust, and wear PPE, the limitations of assigned PPE, and the proper care, maintenance, useful life, and disposal of PPE. Require workers to demonstrate understanding and proper use before performing work requiring PPE, and retrain when workplace conditions, job assignments, PPE types, or worker knowledge gaps make prior training obsolete.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use the work-center JHA, BE occupational health assessment, manufacturer instructions, DAFMAN 91-203 Chapter 14, and local safety office guidance to identify PPE requirements. Supervisors must ensure PPE is provided, used, cleaned, inspected, maintained in sanitary and serviceable condition, and documented in JSTO training records. Cover eye and face protection, head protection, foot protection, hand protection, protective clothing, and respiratory or hearing protection when those programs apply.
